summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of kidney and pancreas transplants, type 1 diabetes, and diastolic heart failure was admitted after developing fever and chills during dialysis, progressing to septic shock. She presented with altered mental status and was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics and stress-dose steroids. Blood cultures grew E. coli, and given concern for dialysis catheter-related infection, the existing tunneled catheter was removed and a new one placed. Antibiotics were initially given with meropenem, then switched to ceftazidime based on sensitivities and to avoid nephrotoxicity, despite a history of cephalosporin-related neutropenia; CBC monitoring was initiated. Her symptoms resolved with treatment and dialysis. Imaging showed severe mitral regurgitation and mild pulmonary edema, managed supportively. She remained afebrile, with negative repeat blood cultures, and was discharged to extended care on a two-week course of ceftazidime with dialysis and close CBC monitoring.
problems: Septicemia due to escherichia coli [E. coli]
Other and unspecified infection due to central venous catheter
Combined systolic and diastolic heart failure, unspecified
Cephalosporin group causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
